domains.name: People
domains.definition: People (incl Family Units). The People Domain contains information about individuals.

domains.name: LegalEntities
domains.definition: Legal Entities (incl. Relationships, Companies, Funds, Charities, Governments, Agencies etc.). The LegalEntities Domain defines the different entities involved in business transactions, services or other processes in any capacity.

domains.name: Documents
domains.definition: Documents (including Contracts, Agreements, Amendments, etc). The Documents Domain contains records that provide documentary evidence or support for business processes including Legal, Transactional, Regulatory, Identification and Commercial.

domains.name: Events
domains.definition: Events describe meaningful events in the lifecycle of various data assets including Mergers, Births, Deaths, Stock-Splits etc.

domains.name: Transactions
domains.definition: Transactions are records of an individual trade/transaction which represents a transfer of ownership or investment usually in return for capital.

platform_findings.finding: LegalEntityRoles stores roles — investor, vendor, client — on the organisation. Roles come from the relationships in force; this model derives supplier, outside manufacturer and certifying body instead.
PeopleRoles stores roles on the person, and uses the plural People where its siblings use the singular Person.
LegalEntityRelationships holds relationships as a concept. DDA now holds relationships as their own records; not reused here.
The Events domain holds no concepts, so it has no anchor. Its definition describes corporate and life events only, and does not cover operational occurrences.
The Transactions domain holds no concepts, so it has no anchor. Its definition is written for trades in securities and does not cover exchanges of goods.
The Document concept's description calls it DocumentBase, which disagrees with its name.
PersonCitizenship is singular where its siblings are plural.
The relationship reads Managed By forward and Invests In back. The inverse does not read the forward verb back, so the pair describes two arrangements under one name.
The forward verb is Investor, which is a noun. A role has been entered in the verb field.
The stored forward view is LegalEntityGP; the roles on the record derive LegalEntityGPs. A stored derived name has drifted from what it derives from.

guide_disagreements.finding: The guide lists state transitions as readable; the call returns an internal error, so the change package carries no preconditions.
